correctness.rationale: For any injective assignment of three distinct permutation images, a uniform n-cycle extension exists precisely for an acyclic directed partial map, with exactly (n-4)! completions by path contraction. Exhaustive inclusion-exclusion of loops, two-cycles and three-cycles yields five explicit polynomial rows. Algebraic summation of these rows proves each expectation for all n>=4. Standalone direct exhaustive and symbolic checks passed; neither finite sampling nor logs serve as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Single-cycle conditioning and consecutive triple-pattern counts are natural, standard objects in random-permutation probability. The theorem gives a complete six-class first-moment phase balance for every n>=4: zero monotone shift and precisely paired nonmonotone shifts, establishing a global cycle-constraint effect invisible to first-order unconditional pattern counts. It is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a numerical gain; the classification is exhaustive at the first genuinely order-sensitive triple length.
